overview:
This 6 day Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour is a guided trip from Windhoek through the Erongo Mountains, Damaraland and the southern edge of Kaokoland. It visits the San and Damara living museums, tracks desert-adapted elephants, sees the Twyfelfontein rock engravings and meets the OvaHimba. It runs all year, costs from USD 3,850 per adult and suits travellers who want culture and scenery more than big game.

The tour travels in an air-conditioned vehicle with a professional English-speaking guide, and park entrance fees, the listed activities and airport transfers are included.

Why choose a 6 day Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour?

The 6 day Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour puts people first. Instead of a single village stop, you spend time with three communities in their own surroundings: the San in the Erongo Mountains, the Damara in Damaraland and the semi-nomadic OvaHimba in Kaokoland, with a chance to learn a few words of their languages along the way.

The landscapes do the rest. Damaraland and Kaokoland are unfenced, arid wilderness where elephants and livestock herders share scarce water, so the wildlife you see tells the story of how people and animals coexist in north-west Namibia.

  • Culture lovers: San and Damara living museums and an afternoon with the OvaHimba.
  • History buffs: San rock paintings in the Erongo and over 40,000 rock engravings at Twyfelfontein.
  • Photographers: rugged mountains, desert light and a sundowner drive in Kaokoland.

What to expect on the 6 day Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour

Day 1 is your arrival, when a Divulge Adventures representative meets you and briefs you on the route. On day 2 your guide drives you from Windhoek to the Erongo Mountains, where the San Living Museum shows hunting, tracking, fire-making and bush food, rock paintings over 2,000 years old, and ends with singing and dancing.

Day 3 continues from the Erongo Mountains to Twyfelfontein in Damaraland and the Damara Living Museum, which reconstructs traditional Damara culture. Day 4 is the highlight for many guests: a morning tracking desert-adapted elephants, then an afternoon at the Twyfelfontein rock engravings.

On day 5 you drive past villages and conservancies, with a chance of wildlife, to the start of Kaokoland for an afternoon with the OvaHimba, learning about their dress, food, crafts and the holy fire at the heart of the homestead, followed by a sundowner drive. Day 6 is the transfer back to Windhoek.

Is the tour suitable if I mainly want wildlife?

This culture tour is not a classic game-viewing safari. Wildlife in Damaraland and Kaokoland is sparse and hard to spot, and the elephant tracking is the main wildlife activity. If big game matters most, ask us to add Etosha, or look at our 5 day Southern Skeleton Coast tour for seals and marine life. Our best time to visit Namibia guide covers the seasons.

faq.q: When is the best time for the 6 day Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour?
faq.a: The 6 day Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour runs all year, and the trip page does not set a season. May to October is the dry, cooler season, with comfortable days for elephant tracking and village visits. November to March is hotter, with afternoon storms that can make Kaokoland tracks slower, so we plan driving times around the weather.

faq.q: Where do you stay on the 6 day Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour?
faq.a: On the 6 day Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour you stay near the Erongo Mountains, two nights in Damaraland around Twyfelfontein and one night at the edge of Kaokoland. The trip page does not name the lodges, so we confirm each property, with its meal plan, in your written quote before you book.

faq.q: Is the Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour suitable for families?
faq.a: Yes, families can join the Damaraland and Kaokoland culture tour. The living museums are hands-on, with fire-making, rope-making and dancing that children enjoy, and there is no strenuous hiking. Driving days are long on gravel roads, so tell us your children's ages and we will plan the pace and stops.
